item.title: VANTAGE-V-AI: Bounded-Memory KV-Cache Compression and Streaming Inference Runtime for Large Language Models
item.description: Autoregressive generation in Large Language Models (LLMs) deployed within extended multi-turn dialogs and autonomous agentic workflows suffers from an acute memory wall. Because conventional Key-Value (KV) caching retains representations for all preceding tokens, memory consumption scales linearly O(N) with sequence length and batch size, precipitating catastrophic Out-Of-Memory (OOM) failures or massive resource underutilization. item.title: Governed Hybrid Agency: A Critical Evidence Map of Cognitive Architectures for Foundation-Model Agents
item.description: Background. Foundation models provide broad generative competence, but do not by themselves ensure grounded action, reliable long-horizon memory, calibrated uncertainty, execution monitoring, or accountable learning. item.title: From Code Completion to Agentic Development: A Survey of AI Coding Agents, Ecosystems, and Evolving Software Engineering Practice
item.description: Abstract Large language models have extended software-development assistance from token-level completion to systems that can navigate repositories, edit files, execute tools, and iterate on test feedback. This survey studies the design, use, and evaluation of these AI coding agents, together with their commercial and societal context. item.description: Multi-agent systems (MAS) now power long-running agentic applications like deep research and coding agents, yet their end-to-end latency reaches minutes to hours. item.description: Automation platforms such as GitHub Actions and n8n are increasingly adopting so-called agentic workflows, which integrate Large Language Model (LLM) agents for tasks such as code review and data synchronization. item.description: Contemporary global value networks and capital-intensive infrastructure projects face an existential crisis driven by geopolitical disruptions, persistent inflation, and the fragile leverage of conventional interest-based debt. item.title: The design and impact of a dual-agent artificial intelligence system in personalised mathematics tutoring
item.description: Digital tutoring tools are increasingly used in schools to support mathematics learning, but empirical evidence remains limited on how diagnostic and instructional functions can be coordinated to provide personalised support. item.title: Delegating or Doing? Understanding User Behavior in Hybrid Human–Agent Interfaces
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into applications, allowing users to complete tasks either through direct manipulation or by delegating actions to conversational agents. item.description: Abstract Assessment feedback in higher education provides fine-grained evidence about students’ specific errors but remains underutilized as a data source for teaching improvement. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder: pathogenesis, epidemiological characteristics, animal models, and potential therapeutic strategies
item.description: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complex neurobehavioral disorder that disproportionately affects military service members. The clinical presentation of PTSD is heterogeneous and may overlap with other psychiatric conditions. item.description: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge.
